files.title: Files
files.emptyText: Open a project folder to see its files here.

search.title: Search
search.emptyText: Open a folder to search and replace across all files.

editor.label: Editor
editor.welcomeText: Your cockpit for agents. Open a folder to work with your project and your own agent.
editor.workspaceOpenText: Pick a file on the left or search with the command palette.
editor.binaryText: This file contains no text and cannot be shown in the editor.
editor.tooLargeText: This file is {{size}}. Files over {{limit}} are not opened in the editor so Kestrel stays fast.
editor.changedOnDisk: The file was changed outside while you have unsaved changes.
editor.deletedOnDisk: The file was deleted outside. Saving creates it again.
editor.conflictMessage: The file on disk is newer than your version. Overwriting replaces the other change.
editor.unsavedMessage: Your changes will be lost if you don’t save them.

bottom.label: Bottom panel
bottom.terminalEmptyText: Terminals start in the project folder (or your home folder) with your default shell.
bottom.problemsEmptyText: Errors and warnings from your code appear here once language support is active.

agent.title: Agent
agent.noWorkspaceText: Agents work inside a project folder. Open a folder first.
agent.startText: Kestrel starts your own agent in the project folder. Every risky action goes through your permissions, and a checkpoint is created before every turn.
agent.startingHint: On the first start, npx downloads the agent. This can take a minute.
agent.privacyNote: Kestrel does not store your agent’s credentials. Log in directly in the agent, e.g. for Claude Code run “claude” and “/login” in the terminal.
agent.workingPlaceholder: The agent is working … (Esc to stop)
agent.inputHint: Enter to send · Shift+Enter new line

stopReason.max_tokens: The answer was cut off because of the length limit.
stopReason.max_turn_requests: The agent reached the maximum number of steps.
stopReason.error: The turn ended with an error.

error.spawnFailed: {{agent}} could not be started. Is the program installed?
error.sandboxFailed: {{agent}} could not be started in the sandbox. Is Docker running? Details are in the logs.
error.authRequired: {{agent}} needs a login. Log in within the agent itself (for Claude Code: run “claude” in the terminal and type “/login”), then start again.

agent.secretsNote: Note: Kestrel blocks .env, keys and similar files for everything that goes through Kestrel. Agents like Claude Code also read project files themselves, though. Full protection comes with the agent sandbox (phase 3).

status.label: Status bar
status.modelHint: Chat model – click to manage models

code.internal: Unexpected error. Details are in the log.
code.not_found: Not found. Was it deleted or moved in the meantime?
code.already_exists: A file or folder with this name already exists.
code.outside_workspace: This path is outside the project folder.
code.checkpoints_unavailable: Checkpoints are not available. Git must be installed and a folder must be open.
code.agent_not_approved: Starting the agent was not allowed.
code.review_conflict: The file changed in the meantime. The view was refreshed, please review it again.
code.sandbox_unavailable: Docker is not available. Start Docker (or Docker Desktop) and try again.
code.sandbox_build_failed: The sandbox image could not be built. Details are in the logs.
code.docker_conflict: Docker refused: it is still in use (e.g. an image used by a container).
code.docker_failed: The Docker action failed. Details are in Logs › Docker.
code.invalid_url: Only web addresses (http or https) can be opened, e.g. localhost:3000 or example.com.
code.mcp_not_approved: The MCP server was not allowed.
code.mcp_connect_failed: The MCP server could not be connected.
code.provider_unreachable: The model provider is not reachable. Is the address right and the server running?
code.provider_auth: The provider refused the API key (or the account has no credit).
code.provider_rate_limited: The provider’s rate limit is reached. Try again later or use another model.
code.provider_model_missing: The model or endpoint was not found at this provider.
code.provider_failed: The model provider reported an error.
code.model_not_set: Choose a model for the chat first (sidebar › Models).
code.secret_file: Secret files (e.g. .env or keys) are never sent to a model.
code.download_failed: The download failed. Check the internet connection and try again.
code.download_corrupt: The downloaded file did not match the official checksum and was deleted.
code.ollama_unavailable: Ollama is not running. Start Ollama and try again.

workspace.trashMessage: You can restore it from your system’s trash.

nameProblem.invalidCharacters: The name must not contain / or \.
nameProblem.exists: Something with this name already exists here.

search.truncated: Too many results: only the first 2000 are shown. Narrow your search.
search.idleText: Type a search term. Folders like node_modules and .git are skipped, .gitignore is respected.
search.skippedDirty_one: {{count}} file with unsaved changes is skipped.
search.skippedDirty_other: {{count}} files with unsaved changes are skipped.
search.replaceConfirmMessage: The files are changed directly on disk.

why.fileRead: The content is sent to the agent’s model.
why.fileWrite: The file in your project will change. You can review and revert the change afterwards.
why.fileDelete: The file will be removed from your project.
why.commandRun: Commands run with your rights on your system and can do anything you can do.
why.browser: The agent sees web content. It is treated as untrusted.
why.mcpTool: The tool runs outside Kestrel and can take its own actions.
why.docker: Containers and images on your system will change.
why.browserControl: The agent opens a web address in Kestrel’s browser. The page content stays untrusted.

rules.title: Manage permissions
rules.intro: Without a matching rule, Kestrel asks. “Deny” always wins over “Allow”. Files with secrets (.env, keys, .ssh …) are always blocked for agents.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Rules are also created when you choose “Always allow”.
rules.patternHint: For files a pattern like src/** or *.md. For commands the exact command. ** means everything.

log.title: Permission log
log.emptyText: Every agent action that was allowed or denied is listed here.

checkpoints.title: Checkpoints
checkpoints.empty: No checkpoints yet. One is created automatically before every agent turn.
checkpoints.noGit: Checkpoints need Git. Install Git to be able to jump back to earlier states.
checkpoints.changesIntro: These files changed since then. Restoring brings back the checkpoint’s state. The current state is saved first.
checkpoints.restoreAllTitle: Restore the project to this checkpoint?
checkpoints.restoreMessage: The current state is saved as a checkpoint first, so you can undo this too.

agentLog.title: Agent output
agentLog.emptyText: Diagnostic messages of the agent appear here, e.g. when it does not start.

agents.title: Manage agents
agents.name: Name
agents.envHint: Values are stored encrypted in the system keychain and never shown.
agents.deleteMessage: The configuration and its stored values are removed.

review.doneText: No change is waiting for a decision for this file anymore.
review.heldInfo: Not saved yet: the file on disk is unchanged until you accept.
review.appliedInfo: The agent changed this file itself. Rejecting restores the previous state.

sandbox.enabledHint: The agent runs in a container. It sees only this project (without secret files such as .env) and its own home folder, nothing else of your computer.
sandbox.directHint: The agent runs directly on your system, with your user rights. It can reach everything you can.
sandbox.baseImageHint: A Debian-based Node.js image, e.g. node:22-bookworm-slim or a mirror of it. Changing it builds a new sandbox image.
sandbox.imageMissing: The sandbox image is not built yet. It is built on the first start, or now.
sandbox.preparing: Building the sandbox image … (see Logs › Sandbox)
sandbox.login: Log in in the sandbox terminal
sandbox.loginHint: Opens a terminal in this agent's sandbox, without your project. Log in to the agent there yourself, e.g. for Claude Code: run “npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code” and type “/login”. The login stays in the agent's Docker volume; Kestrel never reads it.
sandbox.badgeSandboxHint: The agent runs in a Docker container and only sees this project.
sandbox.badgeDirectHint: The agent runs directly on your system with your user rights.
sandbox.logEmptyText: When the sandbox image is built, the output appears here.

notInstalled.mac: Install Docker Desktop (or Colima), start it and check again.
notInstalled.windows: Install Docker Desktop with the WSL 2 backend, start it and check again.
notInstalled.linux: Install Docker Engine from your distribution or docker.com, start it (systemctl start docker) and check again.

notRunning.mac: Start Docker Desktop (or “colima start”) and check again.
notRunning.windows: Start Docker Desktop and wait until it says “Engine running”.
notRunning.linux: Start the Docker service, e.g. “sudo systemctl start docker”, and check again.

noPermission.mac: Restart Docker Desktop; if that does not help, reset its settings to the defaults.
noPermission.windows: Make sure your user is in the “docker-users” group, then sign out and in again.
noPermission.linux: Add your user to the “docker” group (sudo usermod -aG docker $USER), then sign out and in again.

error.mac: Restart Docker Desktop and check again. Details are in the logs.
error.windows: Restart Docker Desktop and check again. Details are in the logs.
error.linux: Restart the Docker service and check again.

docker.title: Docker
docker.tagInvalid: Use lower-case letters, digits and . _ - / plus an optional :tag, e.g. my-app:latest.
docker.chooseDockerfileText: The image is built with the Dockerfile's folder as context.
docker.noDockerfiles: No Dockerfile found in this project.
docker.noProjectContainers: No container belongs to this project (Docker Compose folder or a mounted folder inside it).
docker.removeRunningTitle: Container “{{name}}” is running. Stop and remove it?
docker.removeContainerMessage: The container and its data that is not in a volume are deleted. Images and volumes stay.
docker.removeSandboxMessage: This is a container of Kestrel's agent sandbox. A running agent in it stops. The agent's login (its volume) stays.
docker.removeImageMessage: The image is deleted from Docker. You can build or download it again later.
docker.cancelBuildMessage: The build is still running. Closing the tab cancels it.
docker.outputEmptyText: Container logs and image builds open here, one tab each.

browser.emptyHint: Enter an address above. Pages run separately from Kestrel, with their own cookies.
browser.loadFailed: The page could not be loaded ({{error}}).
browser.clearDataMessage: Cookies, logins, storage and cache of the integrated browser are deleted. Open pages stay open.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.name: Name
mcp.idTaken: The id “{{id}}” is already used. Choose another name.
mcp.oauthHint: Servers that need a browser login (OAuth) are not supported yet. A fixed header like Authorization works.
mcp.secretsHint: Values are stored in your system keychain and never shown again.
mcp.sandboxAccess: Also for agents in the sandbox
mcp.sandboxLocalHint: Local servers run on your system with your rights, also when the agent is in the sandbox. Only allow this if the server cannot reach anything sensitive.
mcp.sandboxRemoteHint: Remote servers run elsewhere; sandboxed agents may use them.
mcp.deleteMessage: Its configuration, stored secrets and tool levels are deleted. Agents no longer get its tools.
mcp.noTools: No tools yet. Test the connection to load them.
mcp.descriptionsUntrusted: Descriptions come from the server and are untrusted.
mcp.localHint: Started by Kestrel on your computer, with your user rights.
mcp.emptyText: MCP servers give agents extra tools. Kestrel asks before each tool call unless you allow it.
mcp.builtInText: Always offered to agents. Each use asks for permission (Browser).
mcp.importNone: This project has no .mcp.json with servers.
mcp.importNothingNew: All servers from .mcp.json are already imported.
mcp.importMessage: From the project's .mcp.json. Local servers will be confirmed one by one.
mcp.logEmptyText: Messages of local MCP servers and connection errors appear here.

models.title: Models
models.emptyText: Add an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenRouter with your API key, or a local model with Ollama or llama.cpp. It powers the chat and autocompletion.
models.byoNote: Kestrel does not sell or proxy AI usage: requests go directly from this computer to the provider you configure.

error.auth: The API key was refused (or the account has no credit).
error.server: The provider has a problem (server error).

providers.title: Providers
providers.name: Name
providers.idTaken: A provider with the id “{{id}}” exists already. Choose another name.
providers.modelsHint: One model per line. The first one is used; the others are fallbacks when it is rate-limited or unavailable.
providers.keyDropped: The address changed: the stored key will be removed. Enter it again if it belongs to the new address.
providers.keyHint: Stored only in the system keychain – never in project files or logs, and never shown to the window again.
providers.localNote: Runs on this computer: your code and prompts stay local.
providers.remoteNote: Prompts and attached code are sent to this provider.
providers.freeNote: Free models: the provider may use your prompts for training. Do not send confidential code.
providers.freeShort: Free model: prompts may be used for training.
providers.deleteMessage: The provider and its stored API key are removed.
providers.modelNotListed: a configured model is not in the list

completion.title: Autocompletion
completion.modelHint: Small local models (e.g. a 1.5B coder model with Ollama) feel the most fluid.
completion.fimHint: Auto uses the code after the cursor if the endpoint supports it, else a chat prompt.
completion.chooseModelFirst: Choose an autocompletion model first (sidebar › Models).

chat.title: Chat
chat.modelHint: Used by the chat in the right panel. Fallbacks come from the provider’s model list.
chat.emptyText: Ask a question. Attach the current file or selection with the paperclip.
chat.attachNoFile: Open a file in the editor first.
chat.attachSecret: Secret files (e.g. .env or keys) are never sent to a model.
chat.attachTooLarge: The file is too large to attach. Select the relevant part instead.
chat.noProviderText: The chat talks to a model of your choice: OpenRouter, a local model with Ollama or llama.cpp, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
chat.privacyNote: The chat has no access to your files: it only sees what you write and attach.

setup.title: Set up local models
setup.welcomeText: This assistant checks your computer, recommends a model for autocompletion and one for chat, and can install Ollama and the models for you. Every step is optional.
setup.honestNote: Honestly: local models are free and private, but for agentic work (larger changes across many files) they are usually clearly weaker than large cloud models. Autocompletion works well locally.
setup.privacyNote: Nothing is sent anywhere for the hardware check. Downloads start only when you click.
setup.hardwareFailed: The hardware could not be detected.
setup.detecting: Detecting hardware … (this takes a few seconds)
setup.cpuOnlyNote: No graphics acceleration was found: models run on the processor. Small models still work for autocompletion; chat will be slow.
setup.noFit: No local model fits well – a cloud provider is the better choice.
setup.catalogCurrent: The model catalog is up to date.
setup.runtimeText: Ollama runs the models on your computer and offers them to Kestrel at localhost.
setup.ollamaStopped: Ollama is installed but not running. Start Ollama, then check again.
setup.lowDisk: There may not be enough free disk space.
setup.installHint: The file comes from the official GitHub release. Kestrel checks its SHA-256 checksum and asks you before the installer starts.
setup.installerStarted: The installer is running. Follow it, then click “Check again”.
setup.linuxInstall: On Linux, install Ollama with the official script in a terminal (it needs administrator rights):
setup.manualInstall: Install Ollama from ollama.com/download, then click “Check again”.
setup.otherRuntimes: Using llama.cpp or a cloud provider instead? Skip the assistant and add it under Models.
setup.modelsText: Choose the models. The recommendation fits your memory; larger models are better but slower.
setup.needsOllama: Ollama must be running to download models.
setup.modelsSource: Models come from the official Ollama library; Ollama verifies every file.
setup.speedText: Optional: a short test generates a little text with each downloaded model and measures its speed. It uses the processor/graphics card for a few seconds.
setup.speedNothing: Download a model first to test its speed.
setup.doneNothing: No model is downloaded yet. You can add models later under Models.
setup.rerunHint: You can start this assistant again anytime (Models › magic wand, or the command palette).

updates.available: Kestrel {{version}} is available. Click it in the status bar to download.
updates.disabledHint: Updates are checked in the installed app only (and can be switched off in the command palette).
updates.failed: Could not check for updates (offline, or the release feed is not public).
